# Merge, Integration, Kanban and Release Rules

Read root `AGENTS.md` and `ISSUE-PR-POLICY.md`, plus applicable mode policy and approved official course/repo release sources. The default path is:

`feature or docs branch → PR to sprint_N_staging → independent peer review → teammate merge → Author post-merge verification → original Issue completion`

A separate authorized release/integration Issue with independently reviewed release PR is required for `sprint_N_staging → main` when the agreed workflow calls for release. No direct unreviewed push or self-merge to `main`. Do not infer deploy or production readiness from staging merge.

**Issue #45 proposed upfront-grant workflow (NOT ACTIVE before its independent governance merge):** A single human approval at **Issue intake** can contain distinct, named action/principal rights for Author implementation/one PR/same-PR corrections, independent Reviewer Formal Review, independently authenticated teammate `MERGE_STAGING` under current live predicates, and Author post-merge verification/Kanban/closure. **The PR Author/Developer is NEVER authorized to merge their own PR.** If the required actor/action grant was already explicitly included in the original Issue decision, do not request approval a second time halfway through. A user-assigned PR review URL also grants that independent Reviewer a scoped Formal Review decision, but not a Merge grant. `main`, release tags, deployment and branch-setting changes remain separately authorized operations.

**MANDATORY Kanban pre-action gates:** Read actual Project #4 Issue item/`Status`/`Period` before every phase and write/read back the factual transition **before next phase starts**: immediate authorized Issue creation → `Backlog`; completed scope/AC/STS plan → `Specified` before branch work; authorized branch/edits → `Started` before implementation; review-ready existing PR → `PR Review` before handoff; independent binding `REQUEST_CHANGES` → `Fixing` before edits; corrected/retested current HEAD → `PR Review` before re-review; **actual independently executed** staging merge + Author post-merge tests/AC/DoD → `Done` before Issue closure. Preserve correct `Period` and manual moves. Missing item, permission or read-back: `KANBAN NOT VERIFIED / BLOCKED`; do not invent history or continue a blocked phase.

## Conditional review-to-merge-to-closure flow — Issue #37 merged; Issue #45 grant amendment proposed

Once Issue #45 is independently reviewed and merged, the user can approve distinct `MERGE_STAGING` (independent teammate), `SUBMIT_REVIEW` (independent Reviewer) and Author completion grants **in one initial Issue authorization**. The grants remain distinct and conditional; merely receiving a Review `APPROVED` message never supplies missing merge rights. Until the amendment merges, follow the prior separate authorization gates. **Never permit Developer self-merge; never auto-merge `main`, tag a release or deploy from a feature Issue grant.**

A real `REQUEST_CHANGES` means Author moves Kanban to `Fixing` before ordinary scoped rework, fixes and retests on the **same unmerged PR** using the existing valid Issue grant, then returns to `PR Review` for fresh-HEAD re-review. A real independent `APPROVED` triggers fresh read-back of reviewed HEAD/base, Review actor/state, binding threads, exact-HEAD checks, required protection and mergeability. **Only the independent teammate with a valid, upfront `MERGE_STAGING` grant** may merge after all gates pass. If HEAD changes, permissions are absent, checks/protection fail or approval is stale, stop and report the exact blocker instead of attempting Developer merge.

After verified independent merge SHA/tree, the Author's scoped completion grant (which may have been given at Issue intake once Issue #45 is active) permits post-merge regression checks, evidence in original Issue, evidenced AC checklist, Project #4 `Done`/`Period` read-back and original Issue closure. No repeated permission request for the same valid grant. Workflow descriptions do not constitute a deployed autonomous Controller.

## Before approve/merge
- Verify the exact reviewed HEAD, applicable AC/STS/DoD, actual tests and evidence, independent reviewer and all blocking review threads.
- Developer/Reviewer must complete in-scope current-status documentation in the same work PR; only genuinely future merge facts belong in post-merge Issue evidence.
- No unstated instructor approval, global SRS/SDS approval, hosted CI or cloud deployment claims.

## Post-merge
- Verify actual merged commit and target branch/head (may have advanced after merge), and that intended feature tree/content is integrated. Run required Author tests against the merged code with isolated test DB, and report commands, environment, SHA, counts and limits.
- In original Issue record completion evidence, update evidenced checklist and Project #4 `Done`/`Period` with live read-back, and close only after a valid completion grant (possibly included in the single upfront Issue decision) and all actual post-merge tests/AC/DoD. An approved PR or merge alone is not `Done`.
- If post-merge tests FAIL, report the exact regression and issue state; a genuine new repository edit after a merged work PR requires a separately approved bounded fix Issue/PR, not a second PR under the previous Issue. Do not manufacture a fix ticket for historical snapshots or tracker-only status completion.
- Release Auditor uses verified live artifacts (Issue, PR, merged staging commit, applicable acceptance tests, versioned course deliverables and real deployment evidence); report `READY / BLOCKED / NOT VERIFIED`, never invent successful deployment.

## Conditional staging merge / completion checks (future Controller automation NOT RUNNING)

**Scope:** only reviewed PRs targeting an explicitly granted `sprint_N_staging` branch. Never automate `main` merges, direct pushes, GitHub Releases/tags, deployment, course submissions or branch-protection changes. A future Controller may route a ready-to-merge request but does **not** itself perform GitHub Merge or decide engineering quality; only the designated authenticated independent teammate Agent may merge after fresh live checks and a valid per-PR/per-Issue `MERGE_STAGING` grant, which the Issue #45 amendment would allow to be included in the initial user instruction.

**All merge predicates must be true immediately before execution:**
1. Author and merging Reviewer/teammate are distinct authenticated GitHub accounts; current Issue↔PR and approved scope, target branch and latest PR HEAD/base match signed grant and expected state. No unauthorised force-push or scope drift.
2. Formal GitHub `APPROVED` review exists from the independent Reviewer and is still valid on *current HEAD*. No newer `CHANGES_REQUESTED`, unresolved binding inline thread, outstanding formal rejection or required re-review. An `APPROVED` relay payload alone is insufficient.
3. Required AC/STS/DoD and current docs/Completion Matrix are evidenced, required build/tests on exact candidate HEAD actually PASS, no mandatory check skipped/failed, and repository's required status checks (including merge queue constraints) are **configured and enforced**. Fetch Branch Protection/Ruleset and Check Runs live. **If enforceable required checks/protections are absent or unverified, AUTOMATIC STAGING MERGE IS BLOCKED.** A manual fallback is NOT an automatic bypass: it must have been specifically authorized for the independent teammate (preferably up front), all course-required gates must still be met, and the live evidence recorded. If it cannot meet binding checks, remain BLOCKED; never interpret an empty required-check list as PASS.
4. PR is conflict-free/mergeable, approved HEAD/base unchanged at merge time, GitHub permissions and course peer-review constraints satisfied. Revalidate immediately before writing and after any retry; a time-of-check race => STOP + re-review/reconcile, not a blind retry.
5. On an explicitly authorized merge, only the independent teammate executes and reads back actual merge SHA, parents/tree, target staging HEAD and review provenance. If content differs from reviewed intended tree or post-merge tests FAIL, mark `BLOCKED`, retain original Issue OPEN and stop dependent work.
6. Author independently checks actual merged SHA and runs relevant build/tests, posts verifiable commands/results to original Issue, updates the correct AC/DoD and Project `Done` preserving Period and closes only if valid named grant(s) for checklist, board and closure (possibly all approved at Issue intake) exist and **all completion gates** pass. A future Controller may emit `ISSUE_COMPLETED` only after GitHub read-back confirms all. Failed tasks remain pending; next Issue starts only if preauthorized, unblocked and dependency-ready.

Current repository branch protection and ruleset state must be observed, not presumed. During audit (2026-11-13), `main` and `sprint_1_staging` protection returned 404 and rulesets were empty; this is **time-stamped evidence**, not a standing claim for future sessions. A future implementation must explicitly validate and enforce equivalent gates before enabling AUTO staging merge.
